headline: Hartwell Building Centennial Celebration Ends in Chaos as Lights Fail, Guests Report 'Extra Attendees'
subheadline: Omnicorp-hosted event disrupted by 47-minute blackout; some guests claim to have met themselves
summary: The Hartwell Building's 100th anniversary celebration was cut short after a prolonged power outage and reports of unexplainable encounters among guests.
content:
What was meant to be an elegant celebration of the Hartwell Building's centennial became something far stranger Saturday evening when the venue lost power for exactly 47 minutes and guests began reporting impossible encounters.

Omnicorp Holdings had spared no expense. The lobby was transformed with historical photographs, a live jazz quartet, and a 10-foot ice sculpture of the building (with no 13th floor, matching official blueprints). Approximately 200 guests attended, including city officials, local business leaders, and current building residents.

The event proceeded normally until 8:47 PM, when all lights and electronics simultaneously failed.

"The emergency lights didn't come on," said attendee Marcus Webb. "It was complete darkness. People were using phone flashlights, but even those seemed... dimmer than they should have been. Like the darkness was thicker somehow."

During the blackout, multiple guests reported encountering other attendees in places they couldn't have been.

"I was talking to my wife by the bar when the lights went out," said resident James Holloway. "I held her hand the entire time. When the lights came back on, she was across the room by the elevators. She said she'd been there the whole time. But I was holding someone's hand."

Similar reports emerged throughout the evening. Three guests independently claimed to have had conversations with themselves. One woman insisted she watched herself leave through the front door while remaining inside the building.

Perhaps most disturbing was the discovery that photographs taken during the blackout - using phone flashes - showed the lobby completely empty, despite over 200 people being present.

Omnicorp Holdings CEO Victoria Chen (no relation to Underground owner Mars Chen) took the stage after power was restored to assure guests that the building's electrical system was "functioning exactly as intended."

"The Hartwell Building has stood for 100 years," she said, smiling in a way several attendees later described as "geometrically perfect." "It will stand for 100 more. What you experienced tonight was simply the building... introducing itself. Thank you for attending. You may all go home now. Those of you who can."

The event ended shortly thereafter. Security footage from the evening shows only static during the 47-minute blackout, followed by footage of an empty lobby for the remainder of the night - despite the event continuing for another hour.

The jazz quartet has declined all interview requests. The ice sculpture was found the following morning completely melted, though the building's climate control records show the lobby remained at a constant 68 degrees.
author: Sandra Mitchell, Local News
